description: An engineering manager must approve the production rollout configuration for a repository security-scanning policy, deciding enforcement modes, path exclusions, rollout timing, and follow-up work with input from QA and security engineering.

shared_context.S1: The company is preparing to enable a new repository security-scanning policy across production repositories.
shared_context.S2: The current proposal enables blocking enforcement for every repository, scans nightly, and begins rollout on Friday.
shared_context.S3: Riley owns the final production configuration decision.
shared_context.S4: The normal release-readiness process requires Riley to check with QA and security engineering before approving a policy rollout.
shared_context.S5: Before Riley settles the configuration, each specialist records any newly confirmed release-blocking finding in the release-readiness decision log.

PF1.text: While validating the scanner against recent builds, Casey confirmed that exactly three legacy repositories—legacy-reports, sandbox-exports, and billing-replay—contain generated test fixtures that create blocking false positives; those repositories must initially use warn-only enforcement, and generated-fixture paths must be excluded. Casey found this during a separate QA validation task and has not yet updated the rollout ticket.

PF2.text: Morgan confirmed during this morning's security review that exactly two repositories—payments-ledger and identity-audit—contain regulated data and must use blocking enforcement, with their first production scan completed by 17:00 UTC on Friday; security must also perform a review of those scan results. Morgan confirmed this minutes ago while checking audit scope and has not yet posted it in the release channel.

acceptance_conditions: The rollout must use mixed enforcement rather than blocking every repository.
Exactly legacy-reports, sandbox-exports, and billing-replay must initially use warn-only enforcement.
Generated-fixture paths must be excluded from scanning.
Exactly payments-ledger and identity-audit must use blocking enforcement.
The first production scan for the regulated repositories must be due by 17:00 UTC on Friday.
A QA scanner-exception commitment must be recorded.
A security scan-review commitment must be recorded.
Both the QA finding and the security finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C1: decisions['enforcement_mode'] in ['blocking', 'tiered'] and len(decisions['warn_only_repositories']) > 0 and 'payments-ledger' in decisions['blocking_repositories'] and 'identity-audit' in decisions['blocking_repositories']
content_checks.C4: '17:00 UTC' in decisions['first_scan_due'] and 'Friday' in decisions['first_scan_due']
content_checks.C6: all(c in decisions['warn_only_repositories'] for c in ['legacy-reports', 'sandbox-exports', 'billing-replay']) and any(('generated-fixture' in p or 'generated fixture' in p) for p in decisions['excluded_paths'])
content_checks.C7: any(('review' in c['detail']) and (('scan' in c['detail']) or ('payments-ledger' in c['detail']) or ('identity-audit' in c['detail'])) and (('Morgan' in c['detail']) or ('security' in c['detail']) or ('Security' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any((('Casey' in c['target']) or ('Casey' in c['detail'])) and (('warn-only' in c['detail']) or ('fixture' in c['detail']) or ('generated-fixture' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: The three named repositories require mixed rather than universal blocking enforcement, and the generated-fixture finding changes the exact repository list, path exclusion, and QA exception commitment.
The regulated-data finding changes the blocking repository list, sets the first-scan deadline to exactly 17:00 UTC on Friday, and requires a security review commitment.
